France–China Double Taxation Avoidance Convention on Income and Capital, as supplemented by the 2013 Protocol (in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-1 to L.561-57 and R.561-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier) implementing EU Directive (EU) 2015/849, as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843; Articles L.123-13, L.123-14-3 and R.123-223 et seq. of the French Commercial Code (Code de commerce) on the beneficial ownership declaration (Déclaration de Bénéficiaire Effectif); Decree of 9 August 2017 and subsequent amendments; PACTE Act Law No. 2019-486; TRACFIN supervision.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (restricted to competent authorities, financial and institutional obliged entities and persons demonstrating a legitimate interest; not fully public following CJEU joined cases C-37/20 and C-601/20)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport and proof of residential address of each non-French statutory director and each natural-person UBO of the SAS
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Chinese notary public or competent Chinese certification authority, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China (or authorized provincial foreign affairs office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; consular legalization at the French Consulate only for apostille-incapable jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Official corporate excerpt (license) and certified copy of the articles of association of any corporate shareholder in China, issued by the Chinese State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: SAMR / local Administration for Market Regulation, with Chinese notarial certification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs or its provincial authorized office

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Completed French Déclaration de Bénéficiaire Effectif (DBE/RBE UBO filing form), signed by the President or authorized attorney-in-fact
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant and the SAS, filed with the French Greffe du tribunal de commerce through the INPI guichet unique
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required if executed in France or before the filing; notarized and legalized if signed abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn French translation (traduction assermentée) of all Chinese-language corporate, passport and banking records
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court-registered translator (traducteur-expert judiciaire) attached to a French Cour d'appel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Translation certificate under French evidentiary rules; no apostille needed on the translator's certificate

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-adverse-media screening of every UBO and director against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, French national asset-freeze lists issued by the Direction générale du Trésor, the OFAC SDN list, and the French PEP arrangements under CMF Art. L.561-2-2; obligatory identification of foreign and domestic PEPs at senior management and shareholder levels; if a PEP is identified, evidence of the client's legal origin of funds and enhanced ongoing monitoring is required; no commercial relationship may be established with any sanctioned or listed party, and any match triggers a suspicious transaction report to TRACFIN under CMF Art. L.561-15.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (national sole-filing portal operated by INPI); business-name search database via Infogreffe (www.infogreffe.fr) and INPI data
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be written in French or another language using Latin characters; non-Latin scripts (including Chinese characters for a 'hotpot soup base' brand) must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet in the registration form, articles and Kbis extract. All accompanying documents must be in French or accompanied by a sworn French translation. The name must not be contrary to public order, must distinguish the company within its line of activity, and must not be confusingly identical to a prior RCS name or a national/EU trademark in classes 29, 30 or 35.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: FRANCE (in a way that falsely suggests official sponsorship)
Court-regulated professions such as MÉDECIN, AVOCAT, EXPERT-COMPTABLE unless genuinely licensed
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a statutory name-reservation system for SAS names before filing. The name availability check is done at the Guichet unique stage. If the Greffe rejects the name, the applicant receives a documented refusal. The applicant may: (1) correct and re-submit the dossier through the Guichet unique; (2) file a request for voluntary rectification (rectification amiable) to the Greffe; (3) initiate a recours gracieux before the Greffe du tribunal de commerce, followed by recours hiérarchique to the presiding judge of the commercial court, to be lodged within 15 days of refusal; (4) in the event of infringement by a prior namesake, apply to the tribunal judiciaire for an injunction action. For a contested trademark application, the opposition must be filed with INPI within two months of publication.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a maximum five-year period under French domiciliation rules, provided the domiciliation agent is a duly registered commercial operator located in France and all corporate records are available at that address. For ISIC 4638 (wholesale of food and seasonings), a virtual registered office is sufficient for administrative seat purposes, but it must be supplemented by a physically declared operational establishment (entrepôt) if the SAS stores, exposes or handles the packaged hotpot soup base. Customs and DDPP registration will require a physical address for sanitary supervision.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate for the registered office (estimated 15–25% in the first 24 months); for any licensed warehouse or food-handling facility, DDPP and EU-external-border authorities carry out unannounced inspection risk estimated at 25–40% per annum because the same product falls within non-animal-derived high-autonomy food import control frequency under Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/625.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-30 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10 (general incorporation and contribution rules); implementing provisions of Book II, including R.227-1 et seq.; mandatory electronic filing through the INPI Guichet Unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) kept by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; filing processed electronically through INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts constituant une Société par Actions Simplifiée (articles of incorporation) registered with the RCS and evidenced by the Extrait Kbis.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum share capital for an SAS. The full share capital must be subscribed by the shareholders; cash contributions are placed in a non-disposal escrow account (compte bloqué) with a French bank until registration, and the release of funds occurs only upon issuance of the Kbis, subject to any lawful payment schedule set out in the bylaws.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION — SAS [SAS NAME]. The undersigned shareholders, acting under Article L.227-9 of the French Commercial Code, after full subscription and payment of the share capital, resolve: (1) the bylaws forming the Société par Actions Simplifiée are approved; (2) the registered office is fixed at [address]; (3) the initial share capital of EUR [amount], divided into [number] shares, is fully subscribed and paid as required by law; (4) [Name] is appointed Président, with all powers conferred by law and by the bylaws, including opening bank accounts and executing contracts; (5) the Président is authorized to complete registration in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, legal announcement, and administrative licensing. Resolution effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Signing of the Articles of Incorporation (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shareholders and optionally a French notaire; subsequent filing through INPI Guichet Unique.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SAS bylaws in French containing the legal form, corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose (wholesale distribution of pre-packaged food products, including hotpot soup base bricks), share capital, share transfer restrictions, and governance. Have all shareholders sign the instrument, either as a private deed or as a notarised deed where an immovable contribution in kind is made. For cash contributions, open a blocked escrow account at a French bank in the name of the company in formation and obtain a capital deposit certificate.
required_dossiers: Signed bylaws (statuts de SAS)
Identity documents for each shareholder or legal representative
Declaration of beneficial owners (formulaire BCE-1)
Bank capital deposit certificate (attestation de blocage de fonds) or contribution-in-kind report
Power of attorney if signed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deed is challenged, rectify the bylaws and re-sign; if the capital deposit certificate is defective, obtain a corrected certificate from the bank before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of a Legal Notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorized by the Préfecture of the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the notice text to the JAL publisher, including the company name, legal form, share capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, and any conditions precedent. After verification, the publisher issues a justificatif d'annonce légale (certificate of publication) to be attached to the registration file.
required_dossiers: Text of the incorporation notice
Company particulars from the draft bylaws
Power of attorney if notice is filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice is refused or corrected by the JAL, rectify typographical or legal discrepancies and request a new publication certificate within 24 hours.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing With INPI Guichet Unique and RCS Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), routed to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online 'Création d'une société' dossier on the Guichet Unique, upload the signed bylaws and supporting documents, declare the beneficial owner, and pay the statutory filing fee. The system dispatches the application to the RCS through the competent court registry for legal verification.
required_dossiers: Online declaration equivalent to former CERFA no. M0
Signed bylaws (statuts)
Justificatif d'annonce légale
Attestation de blocage de fonds or report of the commissaire aux apports if applicable
Identity documents for shareholders and officers
Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs
Registered office proof or domiciliation agreement
Power of attorney if filed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a 'demande de complément', respond within the prescribed electronic deadline by replacing or rectifying the uploaded documents; a non-responsive dossier is administratively closed and must be resubmitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of RCS Extract (Extrait Kbis) and Company Identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce holding the RCS file.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After legal verification, the Greffe registers the company, allocates the SIREN/SIRET numbers, and issues the Extrait Kbis as the official proof of legal existence. The approval is notified through the Guichet Unique; verify officers, capital, and registered office details against the bylaws.
required_dossiers: No additional documents; the Kbis is issued upon successful registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis contains an entry error, file a request for rectification through the Guichet Unique or directly with the Greffe, supplying the correct information; the Greffe issues a corrected extract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food Business Operator Registration and Prefectoral Licensing Activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direction départementale de la protection des populations (DDPP) and the Préfecture of the registered office; DREAL for classified installations if applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: As a wholesaler of pre-packaged food products, declare the food business activity under European Regulation (EC) No 178/2002 and French food law. If the storage facility exceeds the threshold of an installation classée pour la protection de l'environnement (ICPE), file the corresponding déclaration or authorization before commencing storage. Retain the DDPP receipt and any ICPE récépissé.
required_dossiers: Déclaration d'activité alimentaire
Extrait Kbis of the SAS
Floor plan and storage description of the premises
Fire safety attestation for the building
Municipal or zoning clearance for food storage / commercial use
ICPE déclaration (rubrique 1510) only if storage thresholds are exceeded
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DDPP or the Préfecture queries the application, supply the requested technical documents or adjust the storage parameters to fall below the declared threshold; appeal any adverse prefectoral decision within the applicable administrative appeal period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction départementale de la protection des populations (DDPP) and the Préfecture of the registered office; Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL) for ICPE and environmental matters.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Déclaration d'activité alimentaire (food business operator registration) and, where storage capacity exceeds ICPE thresholds, a récépissé de déclaration d'installation classée pour la protection de l'environnement for the warehouse.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL) via the local Préfecture
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a formal full EIA for wholesale distribution of pre-packaged food, provided the building does not meet the criteria of Article R.122-2 of the French Environment Code for large logistics installations and is not an ICPE-listed facility under rubric 1510 above the applicable declaration threshold.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with local municipal sanitation limits; fluorinated greenhouse gas installations must meet leak-check obligations under EU Regulation No 517/2014; packaging waste must be managed under extended producer responsibility schemes; if ICPE-rubric-1510 applies, emissions, odors, wastewater, and fire-water containment must comply with the prefectoral arrêté or general operating requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued after inspection by the departmental fire and rescue service (SDIS), including evacuation plan and fire-fighting equipment; structural and floor-loading inspection for storage racks; electrical installation conformity attestation; occupational health and safety clearance evidenced by the document unique d'évaluation des risques and the company safety register; and compliance with the Labour Inspectorate for workplace access and first-aid arrangements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP) – Portail impots.gouv.fr; company registration via Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (INPI) and INSEE SIRENE.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entity incorporating a French SAS: file formation via Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (INPI), publish legal notice, deposit share capital, and obtain Kbis; INSEE SIRENE issues SIREN (9 digits) and SIRET (14 digits). DGFiP automatically assigns French VAT ID in format FR + 2-digit key + SIREN. Non-established foreign entities directly liable for French VAT must register with the Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and may need a fiscal representative unless reverse charge, OSS/IOSS, or exemption applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope (worldwide profits subject to French corporate income tax, with foreign branch exemption options); not a Tax_Exempt_Zone; Pass_Through_Eligible only upon elective partnership tax regime under Art. 239 bis AB CGI if statutory conditions are met.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: CIT group consolidation (intégration fiscale) under Art. 223 A CGI; optional partnership tax regime for SAS under Art. 239 bis AB CGI; VAT group (assujetti unique) under Art. 256 C CGI; option for VAT on certain exempt transactions; anti-hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD and Art. 212 bis CGI; no US-style check-the-box election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT – Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 85,000 for goods and EUR 37,500 for services under franchise en base (tolerance thresholds EUR 93,500 and EUR 41,250); no threshold for cross-border exports, intra-EU acquisitions, or taxable transactions requiring VAT ID; intra-EU distance sales threshold EUR 10,000 EU-wide.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Phased B2B e-invoicing/e-reporting mandate from 2026–2027: all companies able to receive e-invoices from 2026, all able to issue by 2027; structured formats Factur-X, UBL, CII via Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or approved private platforms (PDP); B2G via Chorus Pro; no real-time fiscal clearance but near-real-time reporting and lifecycle statuses; mandatory mentions and audit trail.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: export outside EU exempt under Art. 262-I CGI; supplier must hold proof of export within 3 months; intra-EU supplies exempt under Art. 262-ter CGI if valid EU VAT ID, VIES validation, transport proof, and EC Sales List. Services: place-of-supply rules; B2B/B2C services to non-EU customers generally outside French VAT; offshore services not subject to French VAT if no French place of supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR
Proof of Exit / Certificate of Exit
VIES/EC Sales List for intra-EU supplies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: VAT reassessment plus late interest 0.20% per month; 40% penalty for deliberate breach and 80% for fraudulent maneuvers; criminal penalties under Art. 1741 CGI up to 5 years imprisonment and EUR 500,000 fine, or 7 years and EUR 3,000,000 for organized VAT fraud; audit period generally 3 years, extended to 10 years for concealed accounts or fraud; joint and several liability for recipient; refunds may be clawed back with retroactive assessments.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Central Bank of France) acting in coordination with the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution, the French Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority) and DG Trésor (Direction Générale du Trésor, Ministry of Finance) for exchange control and balance-of-payments matters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (free movement of capital) and the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code Monétaire et Financier, CMF). Non-resident shareholders may freely subscribe to capital, receive dividends, profit distributions, loan repayments, and liquidation proceeds. No pre-approval from the Banque de France is required for inbound equity or outbound profit remittances. Statutory reporting (Bof/FEC declarations) applies solely for statistical and balance-of-payments monitoring when cross-border transactions exceed €30,000 per calendar month; such reporting does not constitute a control or a restrictiveness hurdle. Profit remittance can be executed through normal banking channels without conversion quota, provided the transfer is accompanied by proper tax clearance (e.g., corporate income tax returns filed) and a valid corporate resolution of the distributing French SAS.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France no longer imposes statutory export-proceeds surrender or mandatory foreign-exchange conversion ratios. Export receipts of the French SAS may be retained in foreign currency in a transferable foreign-currency account (compte de change) or credit-converted into EUR at the prevailing market rate. Obligations are purely declarative: (i) intra-EU dispatches must be reported to customs via the DEB (Déclaration d'Échanges de Biens); (ii) extra-EU exports require a customs export declaration (DAE) with the product classified under HS 2103/2104; and (iii) cross-border financial flows exceeding €30,000 per month composed of trade payments, advances on invoices, or final settlements must be declared to Banque de France using the FEC reporting framework. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; invoicing in EUR or foreign currency is free under French commercial law, although the bank may ask for a signed contract to evidence the underlying trade.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Compte Séquestre) / Operational Account (Compte Courant)
Operational Account and Trade Finance ECA trust account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: HSBC Continental Europe (Paris branch under ACPR license)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account for cross-border corridors

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. French-regulated fintechs and electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Qonto, Shine, and Lydia, as well as EEA-passported EMIs (Revolut, Wise, N26 through EU licenses), can open a multi-currency operational account for a French SAS using digitized e-KYC. Legal constraints: (i) an EMI does not hold a banking license and cannot provide domiciliation, documentary credit issuance, or a full treasury/swaption platform; (ii) UK-licensed fintechs without EEA passport are no longer permitted to provide payment accounts into France post-Brexit and require a French or EU authorization; (iii) strict segregation of client funds applies under Article L. 526-10 CMF, and interest-bearing or escrow features are prohibited; (iv) large trade settlements via letter of credit require an ACPR-licensed credit institution; and (v) the French 'right to an account' (droit au compte, Article L. 312-1 CMF) guarantees access only at Banque de France assigned counterparties, not at unregulated EMIs. The recommended blueprint is a primary EUR current account at a Tier-1 bank plus a digital multi-currency account at Qonto or Wise for low-value disbursements and currency sweep automation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law (Article R. 561-5 CMF and ACPR guidance) permits remote account opening through video identification and qualified electronic signature (eIDAS Article 24) without physical appearance at a branch. In practice, Tier-1 banks accept remote KYC for resident directors; for non-resident directors who are corporate officers of the French SAS, a 'trusted third-party intermediary' (e.g., French notary, registered accountant, or a bank correspondent in the director's jurisdiction) must certify identity documentation. Some conservative banks require at least one director or the company secretary to attend an in-person advisory interview at a branch to validate the business model, supply-chain counterparties, and beneficial ownership structure. Groupe-level AML policies (e.g., Société Générale and BNP) generally impose a face-to-face or video-meeting verification for any beneficial owner domiciled in a FATF-monitored jurisdiction or when opening a capital escrow account; otherwise, when a qualified digital certificate (RGS-certified signature) is used, remote opening is legally permitted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity or UBO mismatch with the French Régistre National des Beneficiaires Effectifs (RBE) uncleared
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete RBE filing receipt; corporate register extract (INSEE); SAS bylaws; shareholding ladder; signed legal opinion by a French Avocat confirming the ultimate beneficial owner chain; passport/ID for each natural-person UBO; and a no-beneficial-owner-domicile-change undertaking.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds concern for capital injection from a non-EU parent or Chinese exporting entity without proven commercial nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements and bank reference letters of the funding entity; executed share purchase/subscription agreement showing transaction rationale; copy of the Chinese SAFE Foreign Exchange Filing (FDI registration) or alternative permit for outbound direct investment; corporate resolutions on the board of the SAS; source-of-wealth declaration signed by beneficial owners; and historical bank statements evidencing lawful accumulation of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Industry or counterparty structured in a commodity-sensitive chain (spicy tallow/palm-oil-based hot-pot base) potentially attracting sanctions or deforestation-control scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Product composition and technical data sheet; supply-chain contract mapping the manufacturer-to-distributor flow; supplier certifications of non-sanctioned origin and EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) compliance; export customs documents for the EU entry; and an internal trade compliance policy signed by a compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Absence of a genuine economic substance for a French SAS acting as a regional distribution channel
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease or domiciliation agreement at a physical French office; employment contracts of directors and commercial staff; French VAT registration certificate; sales contracts with EU customers; warehouse logistics agreement in France; and detailed monthly treasury forecast showing realistic turnover through the operational account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire to a financial institution or region without equivalent AML regulation (e.g., high-risk third-country clearing)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficiary bank FATF-compliant status certificate; KYC pack of the ultimate payee including passport and proof of address; commercial invoice and transport document (bill of lading/airway bill); purpose code and full wire instruction under ISO 20022; and a confirmation that no negative media screening result exists on the payee.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The capital injection from a non-resident shareholder is routed by authenticated SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for interbank credit) to the French SAS's EUR current account at a Tier-1 French bank. The wire must carry the French 'NCO' (Nomenclature des Codes Objets) purpose code for direct investment — typically 'S10 – Fonds propres – Investissements directs' — and the credit reference should cite the share subscription agreement date and registration stage. Where the injection exceeds €30,000, the bank files the BOF/FEC statistical declaration with Banque de France within 20 business days of the month-end. The receiving bank performs origin-of-funds verification and credit-scoring; funds above €50,000 may trigger a KYCC request for the funding entity's annual report and board resolution. If the parent is a Chinese corporate, the sending bank requires the SAFE FDI registration number (or equivalent ODI filing) and the transaction reference must be included in the wire; an escrow account in the name of the '… en formation' or post-registration 'SAS capital' account is acceptable only if segregated at the same credit institution, releasing upon issuance of the Kbis certificate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement of import purchases from suppliers in China/East Asia is executed through (1) the SWIFT MT103 channel for open-account trade and advance payments, with NCO purpose code 'S30/G00 – Règlement des importations de marchandises' or the specific goods trade declaration referenced on the wire; (2) a documentary Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) issued by the French bank on the importer's behalf governed by UCP 600, negotiated against presentation of commercial invoice, full set of clean-on-board bills of lading, packing list, certificate of insurance, EUR.1 or certificate of origin, and a halal/composition certificate for the tallow base; and (3) for EU-destined trade, normal SEPA CT or intra-EU payment channels. All outbound wires require the underlying KYC profile of the beneficiary to be pre-validated for anti-corruption and OFAC/EU sanction screening. The French bank debits the operational account at the prevailing EUR/CNY spot sale rate, debits a FX conversion fee, and releases funds through its correspondent network (typically via a CNH/Fast or CNY Clearing bank in performance of the MT103 order); letters of credit are confirmed at the issuing bank only with the commercial contract and pro-forma invoice as supporting evidence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/CNY and EUR/USD forward contracts with a French licensed credit institution, permitted without prior declaration provided they are performance-linked to the underlying import/export invoices and not speculative, with credit risk collateralized by the operational account.
FX spot contracts (T+2 settlement) for immediate trade conversion, executed through the bank's dealing desk or electronic FX pooling platform.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on CNY/CNH or emerging-market currencies, permissible as cash-settled derivatives subject to EMIR clearing and margin obligations, but generally constrained to hedges of firm trade exposure without physical settlement in a restricted currency.

Currency swaps (FX swaps) between EUR and USD/CNY to bridge temporary liquidity mismatches between an inbound capital injection and an outbound import settlement, subject to the same EMIR reporting framework.

EUR/USD and EUR/CNY plain-vanilla OTC options (call/put) acquired for price insurance of the tallow-based seasoning commodity procurement, allowed under ACPR conduct-of-business rules when the SAS's treasury policy and board minutes document commercial hedging intent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts and profit allocation resolution (dépôt des comptes annuels et résolution d'affectation du résultat)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (Commercial Court Registrar, filed electronically via infogreffe.fr)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year-end plus up to six months (or such date set by the articles) for shareholder approval; account filing made within one month after approval. For a calendar-year SAS, the customary filing deadline is 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-imposed per-day penalty (astreinte), loss of standing to sue, and possible judicial order compelling filing; deficient files may be rejected until corrected.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and financial statements (liasse fiscale; forms 2065/2031 and annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – French tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year company, 3 May (online); for a non-calendar year-end, three months after fiscal year-end. Paper filers must file by 30 April for a calendar year. Online filing is mandatory for an SAS.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: 10% penalty on unpaid tax (reduced to 5% if tax already paid), 0.2% monthly late-payment interest, plus fixed administrative penalties up to €250 per incomplete schedule.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership (update or no-change declaration attached to the annual accounts filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (via infogreffe.fr)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted together with the annual accounts deposit; any actual change in beneficial ownership during the year must be filed within 30 days of that change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update beneficial ownership information for over 30 days may trigger sanctions under the French Monetary and Financial Code (amende up to €30,000 for individuals and €150,000 for legal entities); the registry may also refuse future filings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory when the SAS exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds at year-end: total assets > €4.5 million; net turnover > €9 million; average number of employees > 50. A statutory auditor may also be required by the articles of association or upon request of shareholders holding a specified percentage.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Local GAAP – French Plan Comptable Général (PCG) and applicable articles of the French Commercial Code. IFRS applies only to consolidated accounts of public-interest groups and is not mandatory for a standalone SAS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SAS must answer an annual confirmation question during the annual accounts deposit indicating whether beneficial ownership information has changed. If no change occurred, no separate filing is required. Any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership during the year must be reported to the Commercial Court Registrar within 30 days through a regular UBO update declaration.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders and share transfers (registre des mouvements de titres)
Minute book / register of shareholder decisions (registre des décisions)
Register of corporate officers and their mandates (président and other officers)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $4,000 – $15,000 per year (where a statutory audit is imposed)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible small companies may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject generally to annual turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up share capital, and at least 75% natural-person ownership or qualifying ownership. The standard 25% rate applies above the reduced-rate band. Certain qualifying new businesses, innovation activities, and investment projects may receive time-limited exemptions or credits subject to separate statutory conditions. The French research tax credit is generally 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that threshold. The reduced corporate tax rate is not automatically available to a SAS owned by non-residents.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited; French tax losses generally do not expire after five years. Utilization is limited annually to EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. The portion not utilized remains available for future years. A carryback election is generally available for the preceding financial year, subject to a EUR 1 million cap and statutory election requirements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, filed electronically through the impots.gouv.fr professional area using EFI or an authorized EDI provider. The return is accompanied by the relevant 2058-A-SD, 2058-B-SD, 2058-C-SD and 2059 series schedules. A French SAS must also file the annual financial statements and applicable tax schedules electronically.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; corporate income tax instalments are generally paid quarterly, with a final balance payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return and schedules are generally due within three months after the end of the financial year. For a financial year ending on 31 December, the filing deadline is generally the second business day after 1 May of the following year. Corporate income tax instalments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December. The final balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, the balance is generally due by 15 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN number, registered office, fiscal year dates, legal form as Société par Actions Simplifiée, principal activity, tax office and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the French SAS as the taxpayer. Identify foreign shareholders, parent entities and permanent establishments where requested. Do not substitute the foreign parent for the French SAS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax result transferred from the detailed tax computation schedules, including taxable profit, tax loss, credits and any applicable reduced-rate computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only profits legally attributable to the French SAS. Apply French accounting-to-tax adjustments and exclude foreign-company income unless attributed under a specific French rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting profit or loss to taxable profit through add-backs, deductions, exempt income, non-deductible expenses, provisions, depreciation adjustments, foreign taxes and other permanent or temporary differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Review interest limitation, non-deductible penalties, entertainment expenses, related-party charges, withholding taxes, transfer-pricing adjustments and expenses lacking a French business purpose.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year loss, prior-year losses carried forward, losses carried back where elected, utilized losses and remaining tax-loss pools.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain year-by-year loss schedules. Apply the EUR 1 million plus 50% excess-profit utilization limitation and test continuity of business and ownership-related restrictions where relevant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable result after reconciliation and loss utilization, used to calculate corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure consistency with the 2065-SD, instalment calculations, statutory accounts and any tax audit positions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax treatment of disposals of fixed assets, securities and other assets, including long-term and short-term distinctions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not assume treaty exemption for a disposal involving French real estate, a French permanent establishment or a property-rich entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Movements in provisions, depreciation differences, accelerated depreciation and other deferred tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support all adjustments with accounting records, statutory depreciation schedules and evidence of business use.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certain expenses paid to related parties, including remuneration, commissions, royalties, financial charges and other specified payments where disclosure is required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report cross-border related-party payments and retain contracts, invoices, benefit evidence, withholding-tax analysis and arm's-length support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax instalments paid, tax credits claimed, withholding taxes creditable against French tax and final amount payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credits only where permitted by French domestic law or an applicable treaty and maintain certificates of foreign tax actually paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual summary of cross-border controlled transactions, transfer-pricing methods, amounts and related entities where the statutory threshold is met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose transactions with foreign related parties, including purchases of soup-base products, royalties, financing, management services, guarantees and logistics charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-credit-specific forms, including research, innovation, apprenticeship, patronage or other applicable credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits supported by French eligibility conditions, substantiation files and expenditure allocation records.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filed returns generally attract a 10% surcharge, increased in specified circumstances to 40% after formal notice and potentially 80% for fraudulent or abusive conduct. Late payment interest is generally 0.20% per month, subject to applicable statutory rules. Understatements may trigger tax reassessment, interest, penalties and criminal tax-fraud exposure. Failure to file transfer-pricing documentation can trigger a penalty generally equal to the higher of EUR 10,000 or 0.5% of the transactions covered by missing documentation, or 5% of the reassessed profits or transactions where applicable under the Tax Code.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% French withholding tax generally applies to dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident recipient, subject to treaty relief and domestic exemptions. A qualifying EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption may reduce withholding to 0% where statutory ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, anti-abuse and beneficial-ownership conditions are satisfied. The recipient must generally provide the required residence, ownership and eligibility documentation before payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid tax-residence certificate from the recipient's foreign tax authority and verify the applicable France treaty article, limitation-on-benefits or anti-abuse provisions, beneficial ownership, holding percentage, holding period and entitlement to relief. Apply the reduced treaty rate or exemption only after completing the required French forms and maintaining the certificate, ownership evidence, recipient declarations and payment records. Where relief is not available at source, withhold at the domestic rate and pursue any treaty refund through the French tax administration procedure. File the applicable withholding return and remit the tax within the statutory payment deadline.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties paid to non-residents are generally subject to 25% withholding tax, subject to treaty reductions and potential 0% exemption under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive where all conditions are met. France generally does not impose a broad domestic withholding tax on ordinary interest paid to a non-resident, but withholding may apply to specific categories, including certain payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions, specified financial instruments or anti-abuse situations. Treaty interest rates commonly range from 0% to 15%, and treaty royalty rates commonly range from 0% to 15%, but the applicable France treaty must be checked individually. Arm's-length pricing, beneficial ownership, anti-hybrid, interest-limitation and anti-abuse rules remain applicable.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 150 million: large French entities generally subject to full transfer-pricing documentation must prepare a Master File and Local File where annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets reaches at least EUR 150 million, or where a qualifying related French or foreign entity meets the statutory conditions. Entities meeting the lower EUR 50 million threshold may also have an annual simplified transfer-pricing declaration obligation, generally using Form 2257-SD. Documentation must be available in French or with an acceptable French translation when requested.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no single general-purpose Economic Substance Regulation equivalent to the United Kingdom or certain offshore regimes. Nevertheless, French substance is required under transfer-pricing, beneficial-ownership, principal-purpose, abuse-of-law, permanent-establishment, controlled-foreign-company, anti-hybrid, interest-deduction and EU anti-abuse rules. A French SAS should maintain genuine French management and control, appropriate personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or functional infrastructure, French books and records, decision-making evidence, inventory and logistics controls, bank-account governance, commercial risk assumption and demonstrable functions. A conduit company with no commercial rationale, no operational capacity or back-to-back arrangements may lose treaty benefits and deductions and may create tax, VAT, customs and permanent-establishment exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Tax Returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional concealment of sales, falsified invoices, omission of taxable income, false deductions, undisclosed cash receipts, fabricated expenses or deliberate manipulation of inventory and transfer prices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, penalties generally ranging from 40% to 80%, and criminal prosecution. Ordinary tax fraud may carry imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000; aggravated cases may carry up to seven years and EUR 3 million, subject to statutory aggravating conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president and directors may incur criminal liability for intentional participation, personal civil liability for wrongful conduct and tax liability under the French Tax Procedure Code where fraudulent or repeated conduct makes recovery from the company impossible. Travel restrictions or asset restraints may be ordered by judicial authorities; imprisonment is not automatic and requires criminal conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to declare French VAT, fictitious intra-Community supplies, missing-trader structures, false export evidence, improper zero-rating or recovery of VAT on invoices unrelated to genuine goods or services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT assessment, denial of input credit, interest, penalties generally up to 40% or 80%, possible joint and several liability in fraudulent chains, and criminal tax-fraud sanctions where intent is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors knowingly participating in VAT fraud may face criminal prosecution, asset seizure, civil recovery and management disqualification. Personal liability is fact-dependent and is not created solely by the existence of an unpaid VAT balance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inflated purchases from related foreign suppliers, unsupported management fees, excessive royalties, non-arm's-length financing, artificial profit shifting, inconsistent customs and tax values or failure to document controlled transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, denial of deductions, withholding-tax adjustments, interest, penalties, possible 2257-SD and documentation penalties, and potential treaty relief denial.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable where they intentionally approve fraudulent arrangements or commit separable management misconduct. A mere transfer-pricing adjustment ordinarily remains a company liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Abuse of Treaty Benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of a French SAS as a conduit with no real functions, employees, decision-making, commercial risk or beneficial ownership, combined with immediate onward payment of dividends, interest or royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or EU directive relief, domestic withholding-tax assessment, reassessment under abuse-of-law or principal-purpose rules, interest and penalties, and possible permanent-establishment or beneficial-ownership findings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face criminal or civil exposure if they knowingly implement sham arrangements, submit false certificates or conceal the real recipient. Courts may order asset restraints and management bans; imprisonment requires proof of a criminal offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Anonymous beneficial owners, unexplained third-party payments, cash-intensive transactions inconsistent with the business, sanctions-evasion payments, forged trade documents, suspicious letters of credit or failure to conduct required customer and supplier due diligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Suspicious-transaction reporting failures may lead to regulatory sanctions, while money laundering and sanctions offenses may result in substantial fines, confiscation, business restrictions and criminal imprisonment. Sanctions vary by offense and competent authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be personally prosecuted for knowing participation, facilitation or intentional reporting failures. Corporate veil protection does not protect deliberate criminal conduct. Travel bans, asset freezes and confiscation may be ordered under applicable judicial or sanctions procedures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorrect tariff classification, undervaluation, false origin, misdescription of ingredients, incorrect customs valuation, unauthorized preferential-origin claims or importation of regulated food products without required documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of customs duties and import VAT, customs fines, seizure or forfeiture of goods, suspension of customs simplifications and possible criminal proceedings for aggravated fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for intentional customs fraud or serious management misconduct. The SAS generally remains liable for ordinary customs debt, but criminal sanctions and asset measures may reach responsible individuals.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Sale or import of hotpot soup-base products with undeclared allergens, inaccurate ingredients, prohibited additives, unsafe contaminants, false country-of-origin statements, missing traceability or non-compliant French labeling.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Product withdrawal or recall, administrative closure, destruction or seizure, administrative fines, consumer compensation and criminal penalties under food-safety and consumer-protection legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally prosecuted where they knowingly market unsafe or misleading products or fail to take required corrective action. Civil product liability may apply to the company and responsible individuals depending on the facts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to keep reliable French accounting records, omission of annual accounts, false bookkeeping, failure to identify beneficial owners, fabricated board approvals or unauthorized distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, accounting penalties, refusal of tax deductions, civil claims, director disqualification and, for false accounts or insolvency-related misconduct, criminal sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president may incur liability for mismanagement, unlawful distributions, fraudulent accounts or contribution to an insufficient insolvency estate. Courts may impose asset contribution orders, management bans and, in serious cases, imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Illegal Profit Distribution and Thin-Capitalization Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Dividend distribution without distributable profits, disguised distributions, shareholder withdrawals recorded as loans, back-to-back financing, or excessive related-party interest designed to strip French profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of unlawful distributions, withholding-tax and corporate-tax reassessments, denial of interest deductions, penalties and possible insolvency or abuse-of-assets proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president and directors approving unlawful distributions may owe restitution and damages, face management bans and, where criminal elements exist, fines or imprisonment. Shareholders may also be required to repay distributions received in bad faith.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Form 2065 or required schedules on time, failure to pay instalments or final corporate income tax, or failure to file withholding-tax and transfer-pricing declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Generally a 10% late-filing or late-payment surcharge, increased in specified cases, plus 0.20% monthly late-payment interest and any specific transfer-pricing, withholding or tax-credit penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Ordinary late payment normally remains a corporate debt. Personal liability may arise where a director's fraudulent conduct or repeated deliberate obstruction makes tax recovery impossible, subject to judicial findings.
